facts.statement: Itaboravis fossils were found in the Early Eocene Itaboraí Formation near São José do Itaboraí in the state of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
facts.quote: uncovered from the Early Eocene Itaboraí Formation of São José do Itaboraí, Rio de Janeiro state, Brazil

facts.statement: The fossil record includes a left coracoid, which is the holotype, and both humeri.
facts.quote: se han encontrado un coracoides izquierdo (holotipo: MN 4114−V) y ambos húmeros

facts.statement: Itaboravis is tentatively classified within the group Cariamae based on similarities to the genus Elaphrocnemus.
facts.quote: tentatively assigned to Cariamae (=Cariamiformes), due to similarities with Elaphrocnemus

facts.statement: Researchers noted morphological similarities in the humerus that link Itaboravis to the family Tinamidae.
facts.quote: some morphological similarities of the humerus to the palaeognathous family Tinamidae were also noted

facts.statement: Itaboravis lived during the Ypresian stage of the Early Eocene, between 56 and 48.07 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Ypresian to Ypresian (56 to 48.07 million years ago)

facts.statement: Itaboravis was an extinct genus of land birds.
facts.quote: Itaboravis is an extinct genus of land birds
